meta.description: Overheard tavern chatter, whispers, and gossip from across Le'Choix.

entries.rumour: They say the Lumina Lab didn't burn down by accident. Someone wanted it gone.
The Solvetra Vault has three floors below street level. No one who works there will confirm or deny it.
OOTS aren't allowed to kill. Which means if you run fast enough, you might actually get away.
Heard a lantern agent got taken last tenday. DOL isn't talking about it.
The Lorewarden Emeritus is older than anyone will say. Some think he's been 'renewed' somehow.
My cousin works the east gate. Says the OOTS patrols have tripled since the lab went up.
There's a second stockpile of Lumina Elixir somewhere in Ars Pontaris. The DOL isn't even trying to distribute it yet — they're saving it.
The Illumination Festival is mandatory this year. Last year it was just encouraged. What changed?
Someone at the Lorewarden's office is selling access to old records. For the right coin, you can see texts that were supposedly destroyed.
The new registration forms ask for 'known associates.' That's not a census. That's a list.
Aurevon Beitomy Erstua rode north with eighty NSPF soldiers and no declared objective. That's not a patrol, that's a campaign.
A wanted poster went up in the Intermellum with a half-goblin's face on it. Bounty said 'seditious conspiracy.' The face was familiar.
They're painting over the old moon murals on the south wall again. Third time this year.
An Ars Cultura lecturer was 'reassigned' last month. No one's heard from her since.
The DOL is buying up land in Lunarthorn. Quietly. Through someone else's name.
That solar priest on the Ars Pontaris bridge? He's not just preaching. He's watching who doesn't stop.
Heard the OOTS drilled crowd-control formations in the Vault courtyard last week. What are they expecting?
Shipments from Ars Lapis have been held at DOL checkpoints for days. The mining families are furious but won't say so publicly.
The Vault added a second checkpoint inside the inner doors. You'd only do that if you were afraid of someone already inside.
Whatever they found in the Lumina Lab rubble, they didn't share it. Went straight to the Vault under guard.
Silas Shadowfoot hasn't been seen in the Intermellum in two weeks. Either he's gone to ground or something's happening.
Someone's been feeding Shadowbringer meeting locations to the DOL. The last three safe houses turned up empty before the raids.
There are two monks operating in Solvetra that no one can get a word out of. No one knows their names. They never speak.
Chasley Fanatirela was spotted near the docks last market day. Alone, which is unusual.
The Shadowbringers are planning something big. Something involving the Vault.
Heard the halfling had a meeting in Virelle last month. Came back with something under his cloak.
Du'geshk Maharjuuj cracked an OOTS officer's jaw in the market last tenday. Disappeared before backup arrived.
Corwin Duskwatch healed three people in the Intermellum without asking for coin. People are starting to talk about him like he's something.
The Smuggler's Den isn't where most people think it is. The DOL's been watching the wrong building for months.
Someone tried to recruit me for the Shadowbringers. I said no. Twice.
The gem quotas in Ars Lapis have increased again. The miners are working shifts that would kill a horse.
Three families lost their export licences without explanation. All three of them had been trading with Virelle merchants.
The Echo Veins are getting louder. The miners say the resonance has changed pitch. That's never happened before.
Someone went into the Echo Veins and came back unable to stop humming a melody no one else could hear.
The gems from the deepest Ars Lapis shafts glow faintly even after they're cut. The DOL buys all of them immediately and never resells.
Ars Lapis mine foremen are on a list somewhere. A list of who to disappear if the workers organise.
The DOL doesn't produce Lumina Elixir for our benefit. Read the ingredients if you can find them.
Lunarthorn hasn't had a DOL representative in years. Now suddenly there are two.
Palegleam doesn't show up right on maps. The trees move. Not when you're watching, but between times.
A soldier from the NSPF expedition deserted and came back to Lunarthorn. He wouldn't say where they'd been, just that he wouldn't go back.
There's a community in Lunarthorn that practices lunar rites openly. They've been doing it for years. The DOL has always known and always looked away. Until recently.
Kageyama was built to face Mount Mortifera on purpose. The architecture is oriented toward it. The city is worshipping the mountain.
Mortifera doesn't erase memory. It erases record. You remember perfectly — there's just nothing left to prove it.
The DOL's been sending things to Mortifera. Things they want to stop existing.
Virelle is the only city in Le'Choix where you can say the word 'lunar' out loud in daylight and nothing happens.
Virelle doesn't trade with the DOL by choice. They trade because the DOL controls the roads. There's a difference.
Ars Pontaris looks prosperous. It isn't. It's a showcase. The DOL keeps it clean for visitors.
The bridges in Ars Pontaris are beautiful. They're also chokepoints. Every single one of them.
Ars Cultura has an index of banned books. It's publicly available. The irony is intentional — they want you to know what you're not allowed to read.
The Prismic Scar runs through the centre of Ars Cultura. No one talks about how it got there.
Kaela Shadowsong wasn't a villain. She was erased. There's a difference, and the DOL knows it.
The three founders built Le'Choix together. The DOL remembers one of them. That should tell you something.
Sibling Thorne was an angel. Angels don't usually make good politicians. Someone must have been guiding the decisions.
Myxtiferious vowed never to take dragon form again. Some say that vow is breaking. Slowly.
The drow lineage — the Shadowsong line — wasn't fully destroyed. Someone survived. Stayed hidden.
Kaela Shadowsong's descendants are looking for the Orb. Or someone is, on their behalf.
The Orb doesn't just lock the Shadowrealm. It's a key. The DOL knows what it unlocks.
Lunar ideology isn't heresy. It's history. That's why they suppress it.
There's a symbol for the lunar faith that predates the DOL by centuries. It appears in ruins they can't erase.
The DOL didn't invent solar worship. They repurposed something older and called it theirs.
The Tre Illium weren't three leaders. They were three problems with a very convenient resolution.
Lucien Morvault turned someone into a goat last month for being three days late on a payment. The goat is still in his cellar.
Morvault doesn't need the gold. He needs the power that debt gives him over people.
They say Morvault's contracts are magically binding. You sign one, you can't break it without him knowing.
Morvault and the DOL have an arrangement. Neither will confirm it, which is the confirmation.
Someone tried to pay off Morvault with counterfeit gold. They haven't been seen since.
Lucien Morvault is afraid of something. You can tell because he's been unusually quiet lately.
The Måneklang was played once, at a gathering no one will admit they attended.
The sound from the Måneklang doesn't fade like normal music. It stays in your memory note-perfect.
Someone heard a name in the Måneklang's resonance. A name that shouldn't exist.
The Echo Unheard isn't a what, it's a who. And it's been listening for a long time.
The Måneklang was seized by the DOL at some point and then it wasn't. No one knows how it got out.
A musician tried to transcribe what the Måneklang played. The transcription was wrong. Every time. The paper seemed to resist it.
The baker on Wren Street has been shorting loaves by a quarter-weight for two years and somehow no one has caught on.
The landlord of the Copper Wheel is having an affair with his own business partner and everyone knows except him.
Someone found a body in the river last tenday. The OOTS collected it within an hour and said it was nothing.
The apothecary near the south market mixes sleep draught into his 'calming tea.' Repeat customers, every time.
A cartwright lost his entire stock in a fire he can't explain. The OOTS investigation took one day. Closed.
There's been a black cat sitting on the DOL administration building for three weeks. No one can get it to leave.
The new cobblestones they put in the market quarter? Came from Ars Lapis. Cost twice what local stone would have. Someone's cousin got the contract.
Two children went missing near the old tannery. They came back three days later and said they'd been playing in a house they couldn't find again.
The wine at the Silver Hook is watered down but the owner bribes the right people to keep the quality inspection marks.
A tinker came through last month selling locks he claimed were unbreakable. The DOL bought them all. Every single one.
There's a rumour that someone in the administration quarter is skimming DOL tax revenue. If it's true, they're either very brave or very well protected.
A dog in the Intermellum can find hidden doors. Someone's been renting it by the hour.
The flower seller near the fountain gives better prices to people who ask in the old tongue. She denies speaking it.
Three OOTS officers quit in the same week last month. Officially 'retired.' They were all mid-career.
Someone has been leaving chalk symbols on DOL buildings at night. OOTS scrubs them off by morning. New ones appear by evening.
A street performer was taken in for questioning after his act included a joke about the Vault. He came back out. Didn't do the act again.
The Intermellum smells different than the rest of Solvetra. Older. Like the city underneath.
You can still see where the old moon-temple stood in the south quarter. They built over it but the outline's still there in the stone.
A woman in the east market claims to be able to read what Mortifera erased. For a price. Most people think she's a charlatan. Most people.
The DOL has been experimenting with using Worg howls to produce the Lumina Elixir. The Worgs aren't willing participants.
Lumina Elixir makes you feel calm. Ask a physician why and watch their expression change.
They distributed Lumina Elixir as a free 'health tonic' in Ars Pontaris last year. Complaints from that district dropped by sixty percent.
What's in Lumina Elixir is only half the question. The other half is what it does after six months of use.
The plan was to get Lumina Elixir into Ars Lapis. The miners are restless. This was the solution.
Someone in Ars Lapis destroyed the Elixir shipment before it could be distributed. The DOL is furious.
Kageyama has no DOL presence at all. The city simply doesn't acknowledge them. The DOL hasn't pushed it. Yet.
People who live near Mortifera age differently. Not quickly or slowly — just differently. Like time treats them as an exception.
The Echo Veins sing at certain hours. Not all gemstones, just specific ones. The miners know which and avoid them.
Something lives in the Echo Veins that isn't a creature and isn't magic. It just resonates.
The Shadowrealm isn't another place. It's a layer on top of this one. The Orb keeps the layers from touching.
The Orb was moved at some point. No one knows where it is now. Some think even the DOL doesn't know.
Palegleam changes what you dream. Spend a night at its border and you'll dream of someone else's memories.
A hunting party went into Palegleam three weeks ago. The ones who came back won't say how many went in.
The forest near Lunarthorn never gets fully dark. There's always a faint light, even on moonless nights.
The DOL says Lunarthorn is tolerated. Lunarthorn says they're simply left alone. There's a gap between those two stories.
Virelle traders carry goods that are impossible to find anywhere else. The DOL monitors their ships but hasn't stopped them yet.
Someone important escaped to Virelle last month. Important enough that the DOL sent a letter rather than soldiers, which tells you something.
There's a tunnels network under the Intermellum. Has been for decades. The DOL has maps of the main routes but not the side passages.
A halfling runs the best criminal operation in Solvetra and the DOL still thinks they're looking for a human.
The Smuggler's Den has existed under the DOL's nose for years. That's either luck or they have someone on the inside.
Someone inside the DOL is feeding information to the Shadowbringers. It's the only explanation for how they keep staying one step ahead.
The OOTS aren't all believers. Some of them are just people who needed work.
A high-ranking OOTS officer was demoted last week. No announcement. He just showed up in a lower uniform.
The Vault doesn't just hold gold. It holds records. The kind of records the DOL would rather have under armed guard than in an archive.
Every major debt in Le'Choix traces back to either the Vault or Lucien Morvault. Sometimes both.
The Vault's inner vault hasn't been opened in four years. Whatever's in there, they're not touching it.
A clerk at the Vault was dismissed and escorted out the same morning. She didn't take any of her personal belongings.
The new Vault checkpoint was installed after an internal audit. The audit results were classified.
The Shadowbringers aren't just rebels. They're trying to restore something. Something old.
The DOL calls them terrorists. The Intermellum calls them something closer to hope.
I heard the Shadowbringers have a cleric. A half-goblin. Does real healing. Not the DOL-approved kind.
If you need to disappear in Solvetra, the Intermellum is your best option. Assuming you know the right people.
The sorcerer travels alone sometimes. When she does, strange things happen to lanterns.
Those two monks — Venn and Varr — they move like shadows. Watched one of them dodge a thrown knife without looking.
Silas Shadowfoot has been running operations in this city for five years and the DOL still doesn't have his real description.
The NSPF is loyal to the DOL but Aurevon Beitomy Erstua is loyal to the NSPF first. There's a difference and it matters.
Aurevon went north. People who track troop movements say he took the mountain route. There's nothing up there officially.
The NSPF did something in a village two years ago that no one will talk about. The village doesn't appear on new maps.
Mortifera can make that happen. A whole village, just... not there anymore.
I don't trust the Lorewarden. Anyone that old who's still that useful to power has made some kind of deal.
The Lorewarden has a private archive that even the DOL high council doesn't have access to. He's the only key.
Someone asked the Lorewarden a question about the Tre Illium once. He gave an answer that was technically correct and completely false.
The Lorewarden was at the founding. Not as a child. As an adult. Do the maths.
There are books in Ars Cultura that aren't listed in any index. The librarians know where they are. They won't say.
Three texts were pulped by DOL order last month. At least two private copies made it out of the city before the order went through.
The Prismic Scar in Ars Cultura used to be a temple. Before that, something older. Whatever's in the scar isn't gone, it's dormant.
The Prismic Scar hums during certain celestial alignments. The DOL schedules events to mask the sound.
A junior scholar at Ars Cultura submitted a thesis on lunar calendar accuracy. She was reassigned before she could defend it.
Ars Cultura teaches history the way the DOL tells it. The older lecturers remember the other version but they've learned not to say it.
The light in Ars Cultura's main hall is never natural. It's always artificial. The building was designed to have no direct sunlight inside.
Kageyama's architecture faces Mortifera because the founders of Kageyama believed the mountain was sacred. Not dangerous. Sacred.
You can get from the Intermellum to the docks without crossing a single DOL checkpoint. It takes longer but it exists.
The dockmaster at Solvetra's river port is on the DOL payroll and on someone else's payroll at the same time.
Virelle doesn't have a wall. Never has. They say they don't need one.
The road between Solvetra and Ars Lapis has new checkpoint markers this season. There are two more than last year.
The Ars Lapis gem monopoly is more fragile than it looks. Three independent families control the deepest shafts. The DOL hasn't managed to buy them out yet.
The deep shafts in Ars Lapis go further than the official maps show. The miners who work them are sworn to silence.
Whatever the Echo Veins are resonating with, it's getting stronger. The miners can feel it in their back teeth now.
The DOL ordered a full survey of the Echo Veins last season. The surveyors didn't finish it. They don't say why.
Something in the Echo Veins responded when the Måneklang was played. Nobody who was present will confirm the connection.
The Måneklang showed up in Le'Choix about forty years ago. No one knows who made it or where it came from.
'The Echo Unheard' — that's what the Måneklang played when it was last sounded. A name. Old scholars went pale when they heard it.
The name revealed by the Måneklang appeared in a text the Lorewarden had declared destroyed. It wasn't destroyed.
Some sounds can't be unheard. The Måneklang plays one. Those who've heard it report it changes how they experience silence afterward.
The Echo Unheard isn't a threat. It isn't a god. It's a memory of something that happened before the founding, and it's been trying to remind someone.
There's a shrine to Kaela Shadowsong somewhere in Palegleam. Hand-built, maintained in secret. No one admits to tending it.
The Shadowsong lineage didn't end where the DOL says it did. Someone survived. Went quiet. Waited.
The drow connection to the Shadowrealm isn't evil — it's ancestral. The DOL made it evil in the retelling.
Kaela Shadowsong built the first settlement in what would become Solvetra. That fact is now a punishable rumour.
The Shadowrealm bleeds through in Palegleam on certain nights. The forest knows when.
Myxtiferious never broke his vow. But someone has been asking whether it can be broken. On behalf of someone else.
The Red Dragon Lord's hoard, if it still exists, would make Morvault look like a market stall.
Sibling Thorne's descendants still exist. The DOL keeps very close tabs on them.
The three founders knew the Shadowrealm was dangerous. They disagreed on what to do about it. That disagreement is what broke them.
The Orb was a compromise. Not a solution. Everyone involved knew it would eventually stop working.
Someone offered me coin to find a specific person. The description was vague. The coin was very good. I didn't ask further questions.
A person came through town asking about old lunar rites. Not as a believer — as a researcher. DOL had them picked up before sunset.
There's a phrase in the old tongue that means roughly 'the light lies.' It appears scratched into walls all over Solvetra. New ones every week.
Someone slipped a pamphlet under my door last month. Just two sentences about Kaela Shadowsong. I burned it. I still remember what it said.
The DOL holds interrogations in the sub-levels of the Vault. Not officially. But the screams carry.
An OOTS officer wept in a tavern last week and wouldn't say why. Paid for everyone's drink and left.
There are people in Solvetra who have never seen sunlight. Not prisoners. Just people who found other ways.
Morvault keeps a list of everyone who owes him anything, however small. He doesn't pursue them all. He collects the right ones.
A Worg escaped from wherever the DOL was keeping them. DOL says it was recaptured immediately. The missing livestock near the east road suggests otherwise.
The Vault guards are paid twice what standard OOTS earn. Whatever's in that building, the DOL considers it worth the premium.
Someone tried to map the Intermellum from memory and came up with a district three streets larger than the official footprint allows.
Lunarthorn has been sheltering people for years. Quietly. Not just lunar faithful — anyone the DOL was looking at too closely.
An Ars Lapis gem that passed through three owners all came back to the same mine. In their personal effects. Decades apart.
The DOL's census is not for taxation. Everyone knows what it's actually for. No one says it.
There's a word in Kageyama dialect that means 'remembered by Mortifera.' It's not considered a blessing.
Virelle merchants carry messages that never pass through DOL hands. They call it trading. Everyone else calls it a lifeline.
The Intermellum used to be open to the sky. The enclosure happened during a 'renovation' thirty years ago. The renovation had DOL funding.
The Shadowbringers sent an emissary to Virelle last season. They came back with a sealed case and a contact name.
Morvault has a painting in his study of a city that doesn't exist. Or didn't. Some say it used to, before Mortifera.
If the Vault falls, the DOL's financial records go with it. Every debt, every bribe, every payment. Gone.
You can feel the Echo Veins' resonance in certain buildings in Ars Lapis if you press your ear to the foundation stone.
The Måneklang is the only thing that can reliably communicate across the Shadowrealm boundary. The DOL suppresses it for a reason.
A lunar priest in Lunarthorn says the Shadowrealm has been 'breathing harder' for the last two months. Whatever that means.
There's a Shadowbringer cell in Ars Lapis that the main group in Solvetra doesn't know about yet.
The DOL's history of the founding ends forty years before the actual founding. The gap is not accidental.
Whatever they're building in Ars Pontaris's northern quarter, it's not a civic building. The foundation is too deep and too reinforced.
Someone in Ars Cultura has been copying banned texts by hand. One page a night. For years.
The Lorewarden's private archive is rumoured to contain the actual founding documents — not the DOL version. The original.
A DOL cartographer was disciplined for including Kageyama on a recent official map. The revised version omits it.
If you follow the old roads — the ones before the DOL re-routed them — they lead to places the new maps say aren't there.
The Prismic Scar glowed last equinox. Only for a moment. The DOL had a team on site within the hour.
Virelle doesn't celebrate the Illumination Festival. Hasn't for thirty years. The DOL sends a letter of 'concern' every year. Virelle sends a formal reply. Nothing happens.
Two people came out of Palegleam last tenday speaking a language that none of the linguists in Ars Cultura could place.
Mount Mortifera's peak has been obscured by cloud for nineteen straight days. The locals say that's how long it takes to forget something large.
The DOL is afraid of the Echo Veins. Not of the gems. Of what the resonance might eventually say.
The real reason the DOL wants Ars Lapis is the deep shafts. Not the gems. What's below the gems.
There are maps of Le'Choix that show a seventh district in Solvetra. None of the current residents have heard of it and the DOL says the maps are forgeries.
The Illumination Festival lanterns were made in Ars Lapis this year. Same forges that make OOTS restraint chains.
The halfling doesn't sleep in the same place twice in a row. He has at least six beds in the Intermellum that no one has connected to him.
Corwin Duskwatch carries something that isn't a holy symbol of any known faith. Whatever it is, it works.
The two silent monks appeared in Solvetra the same week the Lumina Lab burned. Make of that what you will.
Chasley Fanatirela was trained at Ars Cultura before whatever happened that she won't discuss.
Du'geshk Maharjuuj fought in the Ars Lapis labour disputes three years ago. He's carrying something from that, still.
The Shadowbringers have someone on the inside. Not a sympathiser. An actual operative. Has been for years.
Silas Shadowfoot knows something about the Vault layout that the DOL doesn't know he knows. That's what makes the plan possible.
If the Vault heist works, the money isn't the point. The documents are the point.
